formats.name: British Parliamentary Debate
formats.summary: Four teams of two in one room, two on each side, debate a motion after fifteen minutes of preparation, and the judges rank the teams first to fourth.

prep.note: Fifteen minutes of preparation after the motion is announced, with each team preparing on its own. University championships allow printed materials but not electronic devices during prep; school and club tournaments set their own rules.

speeches.name: Prime Minister
speeches.job: Define the motion and give the government's first arguments.

speeches.name: Leader of the Opposition
speeches.job: Respond to the definition and case and give the opposition's first arguments.

speeches.name: Deputy Prime Minister
speeches.job: Rebuild, rebut, and add to the opening government case.

speeches.name: Deputy Leader of the Opposition
speeches.job: Rebuild, rebut, and add to the opening opposition case.

speeches.name: Member for the Government
speeches.job: Bring a new line of argument (the "extension") that agrees with the opening government but goes further.

speeches.name: Member for the Opposition
speeches.job: Bring the closing opposition's extension.

speeches.name: Government Whip
speeches.job: Sum up the debate for the government, with emphasis on why the closing government's extension matters. No new arguments.

speeches.name: Opposition Whip
speeches.job: Sum up the debate for the opposition. No new arguments.

formats.name: Congressional Debate
formats.team: Individuals in a chamber of about 10 to 25
formats.summary: A chamber of ten to twenty-five students debates bills and resolutions under parliamentary procedure, like a session of the U.S. Congress.

prep.note: No prep time inside the session. Students prepare speeches on the docket before the tournament.

speeches.name: Authorship or sponsorship speech
speeches.job: The first speech on a piece of legislation explains what it does and why the chamber should pass it.

speeches.name: Questioning of the author or sponsor
speeches.job: Two minutes of questions from the chamber.

speeches.name: First negative speech
speeches.job: The first speech against the legislation.

speeches.name: Questioning of the first negative
speeches.job: Two minutes of questions.

speeches.name: Next speech (affirmative and negative alternate)
speeches.job: Later speeches should answer earlier speakers and add something new, not repeat.

speeches.name: Questioning
speeches.job: One minute of questions after each later speech.

formats.name: Lincoln-Douglas Debate
formats.summary: One debater against one on a question of values: what is just, right or good, and what standard should decide it.

prep.note: Four minutes for each debater during the round (NSDA, Stoa). NCFCA allows three, and not right before cross-examination.

speeches.name: Affirmative Constructive
speeches.job: Present the value, the criterion, definitions and the contentions for the affirmative.

speeches.name: Cross-examination of the affirmative
speeches.job: The negative questions the affirmative.

speeches.name: Negative Constructive
speeches.job: Present the negative case and refute the affirmative case.

speeches.name: Cross-examination of the negative
speeches.job: The affirmative questions the negative.

speeches.name: First Affirmative Rebuttal
speeches.job: Refute the negative case and rebuild the affirmative case, in four minutes against seven.

speeches.name: Negative Rebuttal
speeches.job: Refute the affirmative, rebuild the negative, and give voting issues.

speeches.name: Second Affirmative Rebuttal
speeches.job: Answer the negative's voting issues and give the affirmative's.

formats.name: Oxford-Style Public Debate
formats.summary: Speakers for and against a motion address an audience, take questions, and close; the audience votes before and after.

prep.note: Speakers prepare ahead of time; there is no prep time during the event.

speeches.name: Opening statement, first speaker for
speeches.job: Explain the motion and the main case for it.

speeches.name: Opening statement, first speaker against
speeches.job: Explain the main case against.

speeches.name: Opening statement, second speaker for
speeches.job: Add the second line of argument and answer the first opposing speaker.

speeches.name: Opening statement, second speaker against
speeches.job: Add the second line of argument and answer the speakers for.

speeches.name: Moderated discussion
speeches.job: The moderator asks questions and the speakers answer each other directly.

speeches.name: Questions from the audience
speeches.job: Audience members ask short questions; the moderator keeps it moving.

speeches.name: Closing statement against
speeches.job: Why the audience should vote against.

speeches.name: Closing statement for
speeches.job: Why the audience should vote for.

formats.name: American Parliamentary Debate (APDA and NPDA)
formats.summary: Two teams of two, Government and Opposition, debate a motion with short preparation and no published evidence in the round, relying on reasoning, general knowledge and wit.

prep.note: No prep time between speeches. NPDA: twenty minutes from the motion's announcement to the round, with any printed or electronic materials; after that, only handwritten notes. APDA: fifteen minutes (the opposition's prep after hearing the case, or both teams at motions tournaments).

speeches.name: Prime Minister Constructive
speeches.job: Interpret the motion and present the government case.

speeches.name: Leader of the Opposition Constructive
speeches.job: Answer the case and present the opposition's arguments.

speeches.name: Member of Government Constructive
speeches.job: Rebuild the government case, answer the opposition, and add arguments.

speeches.name: Member of the Opposition Constructive
speeches.job: The opposition's last constructive; it sets up the opposition rebuttal.

speeches.name: Leader of the Opposition Rebuttal
speeches.job: Sum up why the opposition wins. No new arguments.

speeches.name: Prime Minister Rebuttal
speeches.job: Sum up why the government wins. It may answer new arguments made in the MOC, and nothing else new.

formats.name: Public Forum Debate
formats.summary: Two teams of two debate a current-events question in speeches any thoughtful member of the public can follow.

prep.note: Three minutes for each team during the round (NSDA).

speeches.name: First team, first speaker: Constructive
speeches.job: Present your team's case.

speeches.name: Second team, first speaker: Constructive
speeches.job: Present your team's case.

speeches.name: Crossfire (first speakers)
speeches.job: Both first speakers ask and answer questions. The first question goes to the speaker who spoke first.

speeches.name: First team, second speaker: Rebuttal
speeches.job: Refute the other team's case.

speeches.name: Second team, second speaker: Rebuttal
speeches.job: Refute the other team's case and often answer the first rebuttal too.

speeches.name: Crossfire (second speakers)
speeches.job: Both second speakers ask and answer questions.

speeches.name: First team, first speaker: Summary
speeches.job: Narrow the round to the key issues and extend your best arguments.

speeches.name: Second team, first speaker: Summary
speeches.job: Narrow the round to the key issues and extend your best arguments.

speeches.name: Grand Crossfire (all four debaters)
speeches.job: All four debaters question each other.

speeches.name: First team, second speaker: Final Focus
speeches.job: Tell the judge, in plain words, why your team won.

speeches.name: Second team, second speaker: Final Focus
speeches.job: Tell the judge, in plain words, why your team won.

formats.name: Policy Debate
formats.summary: Two teams of two argue for a year about whether the government should adopt a specific plan, using a lot of carefully researched evidence.

prep.note: Eight minutes of prep for each team, used in any amounts before its speeches (NSDA). College tournaments usually give more.

speeches.name: First Affirmative Constructive
speeches.job: Read the affirmative case: the problem (harms), why the present system won't fix it (inherency), the plan, and why the plan solves (solvency).

speeches.name: Cross-examination of the 1A
speeches.job: The second negative speaker questions the first affirmative speaker.

speeches.name: First Negative Constructive
speeches.job: Present the negative's off-case positions (such as disadvantages, a counterplan or topicality) and answer the case.

speeches.name: Cross-examination of the 1N
speeches.job: The first affirmative speaker questions the first negative speaker.

speeches.name: Second Affirmative Constructive
speeches.job: Answer every negative argument and extend the case.

speeches.name: Cross-examination of the 2A
speeches.job: The first negative speaker questions the second affirmative speaker.

speeches.name: Second Negative Constructive
speeches.job: Go deep on some negative positions, often while the 1NR takes the others (the "negative block").

speeches.name: Cross-examination of the 2N
speeches.job: The second affirmative speaker questions the second negative speaker.

speeches.name: First Negative Rebuttal
speeches.job: Cover the positions the 2NC didn't take. Together the 2NC and 1NR are thirteen minutes of negative speaking in a row.

speeches.name: First Affirmative Rebuttal
speeches.job: Answer the whole negative block in five minutes. Efficiency matters most here.

speeches.name: Second Negative Rebuttal
speeches.job: Choose the negative's best path to winning, weigh it, and tell the judge why to vote negative.

speeches.name: Second Affirmative Rebuttal
speeches.job: Answer the 2NR, weigh, and tell the judge why to vote affirmative. No new arguments.

formats.name: World Schools Debate
formats.summary: Teams of three debate prepared and surprise motions in long speeches, with points of information, judged on style, content and strategy.

prep.note: No prep time between speeches. For impromptu motions, teams get one hour from the motion's release to the start of the round (USA World Schools Debate Invitational rules), with only a dictionary and a one-volume encyclopedia or almanac.

speeches.name: First Proposition
speeches.job: Define the motion, set out the proposition's case and its first arguments.

speeches.name: First Opposition
speeches.job: Respond to the definition and case, and set out the opposition's case.

speeches.name: Second Proposition
speeches.job: Rebuild, rebut, and add the proposition's remaining arguments.

speeches.name: Second Opposition
speeches.job: Rebuild, rebut, and add the opposition's remaining arguments.

speeches.name: Third Proposition
speeches.job: Mostly rebuttal: organize the clash and answer the opposition.

speeches.name: Third Opposition
speeches.job: Mostly rebuttal: organize the clash and answer the proposition.

speeches.name: Opposition Reply
speeches.job: A short, fair overview of the debate from the opposition's view. Given by the first or second speaker.

speeches.name: Proposition Reply
speeches.job: A short, fair overview of the debate from the proposition's view. The last speech of the round.
